item.title: Okinawa celebrates restored Shuri Castle hall 7 years after fire
item.description:
Okinawa celebrates restored Shuri Castle hall 7 years after fire
Officials and residents in Okinawa have celebrated the restoration of Shuri Castle's main hall, marking a significant return of the island's cultural symbolByMARI YAMAGUCHI Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 7:13 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
TOKYO -- Officials and residents in Okinawa celebrated the restoration of Shuri Castle's main hall on Sunday, its deep red exterior and dragon ornaments marking the return of a symbol of the island's heritage seven years after it was destroyed in a fire.
The fire on Oct. 31, 2019, destroyed several buildings at the castle complex in Naha, Okinawa’s prefectural capital, as it was hosting a festival. Firefighters struggled for nearly 12 hours to contain the blaze as it spread from building to building in strong winds. Investigators could not determine the cause but considered an electrical fault the likeliest explanation.
“The fire was a tremendous shock to the Okinawan people," Okinawa Gov. Genta Koja said at Sunday’s ceremony in the courtyard outside the main hall. "Seven years after the major loss, as we mark this milestone of the main hall restoration, I am deeply moved and delighted.”
The castle is a symbol of Okinawa’s cultural heritage dating to the Ryukyu Kingdom, which lasted about 450 years from 1429 until 1879, when Japan annexed the island.
It also represents Okinawa’s recovery from World War II. The castle burned down in 1945 during the Battle of Okinawa, which killed about 200,000 people, many of them civilians.
Koja thanked historians, artisans and other experts from across Japan who contributed to the restoration, as well as donors at home and abroad. He called for rebuilding the rest of the castle, saying the opening of the main hall, known as Seiden, is "not the end.”
The 2019 fire destroyed Seiden and two adjacent halls, as well as four nearby structures, while two other structures were heavily damaged.

item.title: Indonesian rescuers race to find 34 missing workers after a deadly candy factory fire
item.description:
Indonesian rescuers race to find 34 missing workers after a deadly candy factory fire
Indonesian rescuers are searching for 34 missing workers after a deadly fire swept through a candy factory west of JakartaByNINIEK KARMINI Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 1:26 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- Indonesian rescuers searched Monday for 34 missing workers after a deadly fire swept through a candy factory west of Jakarta.
Saturday’s fire broke out at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province. Firefighters battled flames for about 14 hours before largely containing the blaze tearing through the three-story building.
About 300 workers were inside the factory when the fire erupted, officials said. Of those, 63 were believed to have been in the hardest-hit area, mostly on the second floor where the flames originated from a cooling unit.
Indonesia’s National Search and Rescue Agency, or Basarnas, did not immediately offer a death toll, but said they collected human remains in 24 body bags for identification through forensic examination.
Meanwhile, rescuers saved 29 workers, five of whom were hospitalized, and continue to search for the missing.

item.title: In Ukraine, the fight to keep winter outside begins with a broken window
item.description:
In Ukraine, the fight to keep winter outside begins with a broken window
As the winter cold sets in, Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities face a growing shortage of window installers as Russian attacks leave homes shattered and families exposed to the coldByDMYTRO ZHYHINAS Associated Press and DEREK GATOPOULOS Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 12:00 AM
KYIV, Ukraine -- For weeks after a missile exploded in front of her apartment block, Oleksandra Horban found pieces of glass in her small apartment.
She threw out her 2-year-old son’s plush toys which were covered with glass shards. Outside her ground-floor home, mangled window frames were piled onto a mountain of debris awaiting removal. Pieces of glass were mixed with autumn leaves on the muddy ground.
“Even now we still find glass,” Horban said. “If we vacuum three times, wash the floor and clean up, we’ll still find those microscopic pieces somewhere, in the bed or in the toys.”
As winter sets in, Ukraine is facing a severe shortage of replacement windows with Russian missile and drone attacks continuing to damage buildings, leaving residents exposed to the cold. Temperatures in Kyiv fell to minus 20 degrees Celsius (minus 4 degrees Fahrenheit) last winter.
Government assistance can take months, skilled installers are in short supply and replacement costs have soared, hitting low-income districts near industrial zones hardest.
Horban lives in a Soviet-era “groundscraper” - an enormous horizontal apartment block in the Ukrainian capital. A missile blast in October damaged a vertical section of apartments and shattered hundreds of facade windows.
Most shattered windows have been temporarily covered with fiberboard or tarps. Some boards have small openings fitted with Plexiglas to let daylight into apartments.
New windows in Horban’s apartment would cost about $1,700, more than three times the country’s average salary. Government compensation can take three to four months.

item.title: Air alert sounds hours after attack on Russia-bound ship in the Gulf of Finland
item.description:
Air alert sounds hours after attack on Russia-bound ship in the Gulf of Finland
The governor of Kaliningrad says a rare air alert sounded in the Russian exclave near Poland and LithuaniaByThe Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 7:14 AM
Share
KYIV, Ukraine -- A rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there.
The alert late Saturday in Kaliningrad came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, which is a key base for Russia's Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday.
Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed. But The Associated Press couldn't immediately verify the authenticity of the images.
According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022.
The Kaliningrad governor, Alexei Bezprozvannykh, said that “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 kilometers (105 miles) northeast of Baltiysk.
On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defenses working there during the night. They featured photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky, with crackling sounds heard in the background.
Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, that showed clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, while an orange haze glowed on the horizon. They told Russian state media that the photo “had nothing to do with the region.”
As of Sunday morning, Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

item.title: Audience evacuated from Don Toliver concert after substance released in the crowd
item.description:
Audience evacuated from Don Toliver concert after substance released in the crowd
British police have evacuated over 12,000 fans from a Don Tolliver concert after an unknown substance was released in the crowdByThe Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 3:48 AM
LONDON -- More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from a concert by American rapper Don Toliver after an unknown substance was released in the crowd, British police said Monday.
Greater Manchester Police said officers were called around 10 p.m. (2200 GMT) Sunday to the Co-op Live arena after reports of people being affected by a substance, initially believed to be tear gas. Footage shared on social media appeared to show concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths as they left the venue.
The force declared a “major incident,” which allows different emergency services to coordinate their response.
One person was taken to a hospital and more than 50 were assessed at the scene, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms, the North West Ambulance Service said.
It said “decontamination is being carried out as a precaution” at the venue.

item.title: What to know about tear gas and reproductive health, as concerns are raised in France
item.description:
What to know about tear gas and reproductive health, as concerns are raised in France
French activists and lawmakers are demanding after recent protests that police stop using tear gas because of rising concerns about menstrual changes and reproductive health issuesBySYLVIE CORBET Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 7:07 AM
Share
PARIS -- French activists and lawmakers are demanding after recent street protests that authorities suspend the use of tear gas to disperse crowds over concerns it's caused menstrual changes and other reproductive health problems, though scientists have not confirmed a medical connection.
The demands come after police used tear gas during student protests and demonstrations over the cost of living, some marred by violence. Some women reported painful cramps, unexpected bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after exposure, and an advocacy group says it has collected more than 10,000 complaints. Opposition lawmakers are seeking a ban and independent research into possible health effects.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has rejected the calls, saying police use of tear gas is essential to crowd control as an alternative to using more dangerous weapons.
Here’s what is known — and what is not — about tear gas and reproductive health.
Tear gas grenades used by French police contain CS, a chemical irritant that affects the eyes, skin and respiratory tract. CS is a crystalline powder dispersed into the air as fine particles. Its effects depend upon how much is used and how long people are exposed to it.
Those exposed during the protests include peaceful demonstrators — including children, pregnant women and older people — and residents near the sites of protest marches.
Mélina Galland, 24, was working as an independent photographer during Oct. 17 protests in Paris that were marred by rioting and looting. She wore a double surgical mask along with a diving mask when tear gas grenades were fired.

item.title: Turkish authorities search for lion spotted on outskirts of Istanbul
item.description:
Turkish authorities search for lion spotted on outskirts of Istanbul
Police and animal welfare teams in Istanbul are searching for a female lion seen prowling the city’s outskirtsByThe Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 2:09 AM
Share
ISTANBUL -- Police and animal welfare teams in Istanbul are searching for a female lion seen prowling the city’s outskirts, Turkish officials said Monday.
A resident in the Uskumrukoy neighborhood spotted the animal on Sunday evening, and it was later seen on security camera footage. Uskumrukoy is on the northern edge of Istanbul’s European side, an area surrounded by forests.
“The location of the lion has been identified, and the necessary care is being taken to capture it alive,” the Istanbul governor’s office said in a statement posted on social media.
Grainy images published by the Demiroren News Agency showed the lion walking through a grassy area. It was unclear where the lion came from, but some media reports suggested it had escaped from a nearby home.

item.title: Poland says Russia twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper
item.description:
Poland says Russia twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper
Denmark expelled a Russian official after it said it thwarted an alleged plot.ByCLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 1:12 PM
Share
WARSAW, Poland -- Denmark has expelled a Russian official after it said it had thwarted an alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil. The case took a new twist Sunday when Polish authorities revealed that the same man was allegedly targeted by Moscow's intelligence services last summer in Poland.
Denmark is expected to ask the European Union this week for more decisive action stemming from the case, perhaps restricting Russian citizens from entering and traveling freely within the EU. Poland said it would support such measures.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia’s threats were becoming more real, reaching EU soil as the bloc continues supporting Ukraine as Moscow's full-scale invasion nears the five-year mark.
The case involves Albert Vasiliev, a rapper who performs under the name Kyivstoner and holds Ukrainian and U.S. citizenship, according to Danish media.
The assassination attempt in Denmark was planned for Sept. 25 during a concert north of Copenhagen, according to the Danish Security and Intelligence Service, known by its acronym PET. It said the plot was “planned and initiated by Russian intelligence services.”
The plot was thwarted by authorities, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday. PET said two men were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service in operating in Denmark. They were linked to Loyal to Familia, it said, a banned gang known for “extensive, serious and violent criminal activity.”
Russia dismissed the allegations through its embassy in Copenhagen, saying the accusations were unsubstantiated.
Denmark responded by expelling Russia’s defense attaché.

item.title: Carney enlists fake Trump for laughs at Canada's annual press gallery dinner
item.description:
Carney enlists fake Trump for laughs at Canada's annual press gallery dinner
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shared the stage with a fake Donald Trump and two versions of himself Saturday, enlisting comedians to help roast the U.S. president and Canadian politicians at an annual dinner with journalistsByThe Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 8:41 PM
Share
OTTAWA, Ontario -- Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shared the stage with a fake Donald Trump and another version of himself this weekend, enlisting comedians to help roast the U.S. president and Canadian politicians at an annual dinner with journalists.
“I am pressing the emergency comedy button,” Carney said Saturday as comedian Mark McKinney appeared impersonating the prime minister, followed by Mark Critch playing Trump.
Critch recreated Trump’s trademark forceful handshake, exchanging grips with Carney and McKinney onstage.
Carney also poked fun at Trump’s lavish makeover of the Oval Office.
“This is a tough room. And I’ve been in the Oval Office. Alone. With its new interior decorator,” Carney said.
Since returning to the White House, Trump has filled the Oval Office with gold accents, gilded decorations and portraits.
The annual Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner is Canada’s version of a Washington political roast, where politicians and journalists trade jokes and insults.

item.title: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones hit Russian warship at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
item.description:
Suspected Ukrainian sea drones hit Russian warship at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
The sea drone strike triggered an explosion and fire in Benghazi.BySAMY MAGDY Associated PressNovember 22, 2026, 10:28 AM
Share
CAIRO -- A suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship Sunday at a naval base in Libya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.
The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said.
They said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.
The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.
Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictator Moammar Gadhafi, who was later killed, in 2011. A U.N.-supported government is based in Tripoli and a rival administration is located in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
The eastern Libya-based government said in a statement that the strike Sunday caused an explosion and fire at the base, which was later extinguished.
The Almasar satellite television channel aired footage showing a vessel erupting into flames. It said the Libyan navy rescued the crew of the Maltese-flagged ship. A corvette warship is smaller than a frigate or destroyer and is built to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.
